model_organism.citation: WD40 repeat and FYVE domain containing 3 is essential for cardiac development (PMID: 30428088)
phenotypes: Embryonic and neonatal lethality
Congenital heart defects: membranous VSD, aortic overriding, DORV
Thinning of ventricular wall, ventricular dilation, disorganized trabeculation at E14.5
Reduced cardiomyocyte proliferation with enhanced p21 expression
Diminished cardiomyocyte differentiation (reduced Myh6, MLC2v, Nkx2-5, Mef2c)
Reduced Notch1 intracellular domain, Hes1 and Hey1; enhanced full-length Notch1
Apoptosis unaltered; no autophagy alteration in heart

model_organism.citation: Autophagy linked FYVE (Alfy/WDFY3) is required for establishing neuronal connectivity in the mammalian brain (PMID: 27648578)
phenotypes: Failure of axonal tract formation throughout brain and spinal cord
Disrupted formation of major forebrain commissures
Disrupted localization of glial guidepost cells
Attenuated axon outgrowth in response to Netrin-1
Phenotype consistent with axon guidance failure

model_organism.citation: Huntington's Disease Pathogenesis Is Modified In Vivo by Alfy/Wdfy3 and Selective Macroautophagy (PMID: 31899071)

Accelerated accumulation of aggregated mutant HTT in the adult brain

biological.citation: Dragich et al. 2019 - Pathogenic WDFY3 variants cause neurodevelopmental disorders and opposing effects on brain size (PMID: 31327001)
biological.summary: Proliferating cortical neural progenitors in human embryonic brain highly express WDFY3. Wdfy3-haploinsufficient mice show Wnt-pathway dysregulation, macrocephaly, and deficits in motor coordination and associative learning. Heterozygous mostly de novo variants (9 truncating, 4 missense) in 13 individuals cause neurodevelopmental delay. A PH-domain missense variant was associated with microcephaly.

biological.citation: Orosco et al. 2014 - Loss of Wdfy3 in mice alters cerebral cortical neurogenesis reflecting aspects of the autism pathology (PMID: 25198012)
biological.summary: Loss of Wdfy3 in mice causes a regionally enlarged cerebral cortex and migration defects of cortical projection neurons. Wdfy3 regulates neural progenitor divisions and neural migration in the developing brain.

biological.citation: WDFY3 mutation alters laminar position and morphology of cortical neurons (PMID: 35733184)
biological.summary: MADM mosaic analysis in Wdfy3 mutant mice shows a cell-autonomous requirement of WDFY3 for laminar positioning of cortical projection neurons. WDFY3 loss also alters dendritic arborization and synaptic density and morphology.

biological.citation: Drosophila WDFY3/Bchs overexpression impairs neural function (PMID: 40000652)
biological.summary: Overexpressing the Drosophila WDFY3 ortholog Bchs in glia or neurons impaired autophagy and locomotion. Glial overexpression increased VNC size and glial nuclei number. RNA-seq found 79 overlapping differentially expressed genes, and neuronal overexpression enriched autophagy and mitochondrial gene ontology categories.

biological.citation: WD40 repeat and FYVE domain containing 3 is essential for cardiac development (PMID: 30428088)
biological.summary: Wdfy3 is expressed in the developing mouse heart, peaking at E12.5, and co-localizes and physically interacts with full-length Notch1. Wdfy3 loss causes congenital heart defects, reduced NICD/Hes1/Hey1, reduced proliferation with raised p21, and reduced cardiomyocyte differentiation, with no autophagy alteration detected.

biological.citation: Wdfy3 regulates glycophagy, mitophagy, and synaptic plasticity (PMID: 34187232)
biological.summary: Wdfy3 haploinsufficiency in mice decreases mitophagy, leaving altered mitochondria with reduced synaptic localization and decreased synaptic density. It also impairs glycogen degradation (glycophagy), causing brain glycogen deposits and cerebellar hypoplasia.

biological.citation: Autophagy-linked FYVE containing protein WDFY3 interacts with TRAF6 and modulates RANKL-induced osteoclastogenesis (PMID: 27330028)
biological.summary: WDFY3 interacts with TRAF6 and is expressed at the neonatal growth plate and in osteoclasts. WDFY3-deficient macrophages show TRAF6 upregulation, increased RANKL-induced NF-κB signaling, enhanced osteoclast differentiation, and greater bone loss in vivo.

biological.citation: Macrophage WDFY3 mitigates autoimmunity by enhancing efferocytosis and suppressing T cell activation in mice (PMID: 41027899)
biological.summary: Myeloid Wdfy3 knockout impairs macrophage efferocytosis, increases MHC-II antigen presentation and CD4+ T cell activation, and exacerbates autoimmunity. WDFY3 overexpression enhances efferocytosis and mitigates autoimmunity.

biological.citation: A rare genetic variant confers resistance to neurodegeneration across multiple neurological disorders by augmenting selective autophagy (PMID: 40945514)
biological.summary: A rare WDFY3 SNP was identified as a modifier delaying Huntington's disease onset by up to 23 years. The orthologous SNP in mice is neuroprotective in two HD models and increases Alfy protein expression. Alfy overexpression also protects against phospho-α-synuclein and AT8-positive tau toxicity.

biological.citation: ASHG 2023 - Opioid Overdose Death and Gene Dysregulation: A Transcriptome-wide Association Study in Nucleus Accumbens
biological.summary: WDFY3 was differentially expressed with opioid overdose death in human nucleus accumbens. It was one of only 3 genes (with CITED2 and ARL4D) that also overlapped significant genes in the prefrontal cortex meta-analysis.
